claude_only.name: What treatment applies to a source element that neither the include nor the exclude set names?
When an include path and an exclude path both match one element, which prevails and on what rule?
Which elements must survive selection for the output to remain usable, and what happens when the policy would remove them?
How is an element treated that was added to the source after this shape was authored?
Which path grammar and grammar version does this shape use to address source elements?
How is an element located when the source is not a JSON tree, such as a tabular column, an RDF triple, a binary region or a span of free text?
How does an address stay resolvable when the source element is renamed, moved or occurs many times?
Which path constructs are forbidden because their result is non-deterministic or unbounded?
Which technique is applied to this element and from which governed technique vocabulary is its name drawn?
Which parameters fully determine the transformed value, and may those parameters themselves be disclosed?
Is the transformation deterministic across separate requests, and what does that imply for linkability?
Which technique-and-element combinations are refused outright regardless of who is asking?
Is this treatment reversible, and which party could reverse it under which separate instrument?
Where is the pseudonym or code namespace defined, and is it shared with any other shape?
What must never be embedded in or derivable from a disclosed code or token?
How is the irreversibility claim evidenced rather than merely asserted?
Which predicate decides the set of records in an output, and over which attributes is it stated?
Does membership in the released record set by itself reveal a sensitive fact about a subject?
What minimum and maximum record counts apply to an output, and which model owns those floors?
How is record scope stated when the source is a stream or an unbounded collection?
Which dimensions are kept in the summary and at what level of each hierarchy?
Which measures are computed, and with what rounding or perturbation applied to each?
Over which period is the summary computed, and may a recipient recombine periods?
Which privacy floor or budget instrument governs this grain, and where is it maintained?
Under what test is one shape judged to disclose no more than another?
How are two applicable shapes merged, and is the result guaranteed no wider than either input?
Which merges are undefined or unsafe and must be refused rather than approximated?
How does merging two shapes differ from deciding which of two policies prevails?
Which inputs must be pinned for a template to be reproducible byte for byte?
Over which canonical form is the template fingerprint computed, and with which algorithm?
Which part of a template may be shown to a prospective recipient before any authorization exists?
When must a template be recompiled instead of reused?
To which source schema or data contract version is this shape bound, and how strictly?
Which selection paths currently fail to resolve against the bound schema version?
What happens when the source adds an element this shape has never classified?
How is drift detected, how often is the check run, and when was it last run?
In which encodings is this shape approved to be served, and is the disclosed content identical in each?
Does the encoding let a recipient distinguish an omitted element from one present but masked or null?
Which encoding-level metadata such as field order, annotations, comments or provenance headers leaves with the output?
How is a holder-selected disclosure encoding constrained by an issuer-fixed shape?
Which facts does a non-empty response reveal even when every value in it is masked?
Does the count, ordering or structural padding of a response leak an attribute?
Do error, refusal and empty-result responses differ in a way that discloses the withheld value?
Which of these residual channels are accepted as tolerable, and on whose authority?
What is the target of this binding, and which model owns that target?
Which recipient class does the binding serve, and how is that class defined without copying party records?
From when until when is the binding effective, and what governs an output already served under it?
Which authority must exist for this binding to be publishable at all, and what happens if it is absent?
Which condition operands does this shape use, and from which governed operand vocabulary are they drawn?
Which attribute values must an evaluator be able to obtain for a condition to be decidable?
Where does declaring a condition end and deciding it begin?
Which conditions are mandatory for applicability and which are advisory?
For each referenced sensitivity class, what is the weakest treatment a shape may apply?
Which classification scheme and version does the matrix key on, and how are keys resolved?
How is a shape checked against the matrix, and what constitutes a violation?
What happens to existing shapes when an element is reclassified upward?
Which regime prescribes a fixed output shape for this data, and what exactly does it prescribe?
In which territories and sectors does that prescription bind, and what shape applies elsewhere?
When two regimes prescribe incompatible shapes for one recipient, what is recorded and who resolves it?
How is a regime claim evidenced so it can be re-checked when the law changes?
What identifiability role is assigned to each selected element, and from which terminology?
Which auxiliary datasets and adversary capabilities were assumed when assigning quasi-identifier status?
How does an element's role raise the minimum treatment required for it?
Which elements are deliberately left unassigned, and why is that defensible?
Which assurance method is claimed for this shape, and against which standard?
Who made the determination, when, and for how long does it remain valid?
Where is the supporting evidence held, and what does this model deliberately not hold?
What invalidates the claim, and how must the shape behave while it is invalid?
Which other shapes may be served over the same subjects to the same recipient class?
Which elements act as join keys across shapes, and how is that overlap controlled?
How many times may this shape be served over one population before the combined disclosure exceeds the claim?
How is a change in the surrounding release set detected after this shape was approved?
Which external policy-language terms correspond to this model's selection, treatment and grain concepts?
Which local concepts have no external equivalent and therefore require a profile?
Which conformance claims are explicitly not made, and what evidence would be needed to make them?
How is the crosswalk kept current when a mapped standard is revised?
Which elements does the issuer make selectively disclosable, and which are always present?
Who is accountable for the final disclosed shape when the holder makes the selection?
How does a protocol's per-claim digest mechanism relate to this model's template fingerprint?
Which parts of a governed shape cannot be expressed in a holder-selected protocol at all?
Which projection of the policy record is published for unauthenticated browsing?
Which parts of a policy record are withheld because publishing them would assist an attacker?
How does a prospective recipient assess a shape without receiving any instance data?
Which projection does a reviewer, auditor or supervisory authority receive, and on what basis?
Is this change narrowing, widening or orthogonal with respect to what leaves?
Which compiled templates, bindings and recipients are affected by the change?
What must be satisfied before a widening change may take effect, and who decides that?
How is a change treated when the policy text is unchanged but the treatment matrix or path grammar moved beneath it?
Which values must be emitted alongside a served output so its shape can be reconstructed later?
Which model records those emitted values, and what is this model's obligation limited to?
For how long must a superseded template stay resolvable, and what remains when it does not?
How are compilation time, effective time and disclosure time kept distinct in the emitted values?
Which observable signals indicate that this shape may now under-protect?
What is the safe interim behaviour between detecting a signal and resolving it?
Which model executes the resulting withdrawal or supersession, and what is handed to it?
How is a long absence of signals distinguished from a shape nobody is monitoring?

grok_only.name: What grain may leave under this policy: record-level subset, named summary, aggregate-only, or a documented hybrid?
If grain is summary, which named summary mode applies (for example FHIR true/text/data/count, or a locally named card)?
Are instance-level records permitted to leave at all, or only derived statistics?
Which NIST SP 800-188 data-sharing model does this grain align to: publish de-identified data, synthetic data, query interface, or protected enclave — as alignment, not conformance?
Which source paths (WM-DAT-004) remain as grouping dimensions in the aggregate output?
Which aggregate functions and measures are permitted (count, sum, mean, histogram buckets, none)?
What temporal grain and inclusive period bound the rollup (RFC 3339 start/end, or calendar grain such as year/month)?
Which WM-XCT-005 cohort/privacy-floor identifier must hold before this aggregate may be served?
Is the path list an allowlist (include), a denylist (exclude), or a mix with explicit default treatment for unspecified paths?
Which path expressions (JSON Pointer, XPath, GraphQL path, FHIR element, OData path) are included and excluded, each bound to a WM-DAT-004 source schema?
What happens to a source path not named in either list: omit, redact-placeholder, deny-the-whole-request, or pass-through?
Does an empty include list mean 'no fields' (JSON:API) or 'unspecified / server default' (OData/JSON:API when fields[TYPE] absent)?
Which paths MUST still appear to keep the payload schema-valid (FHIR mandatory/modifier elements), even if not selected?
Which navigation/relationship paths may be expanded, and to what maximum depth?
Does each expanded type use this policy, a nested projection-policy reference, or inherit parent treatments?
For hierarchical XML/JSON resources, is a content-selector (XPath/JSONPath) used to name the nodes whose shape is governed, analogous to XACML multiple:content-selector?
If the client asks for less than the policy maximum, is the narrower set served (always allowed) or must the full policy shape be served?
If the client asks for more than the policy maximum, is the request clipped to the maximum, rejected, or (non-conformant) expanded?
May the server add unsolicited fields (OData MAY) or is that forbidden (JSON:API MUST NOT), and is that choice recorded as an interoperability alignment?
Which ISO/IEC 20889 technique class (or NIST SP 800-188 technique) does this rule align to?
What exact ISO/IEC 20889 clause or term is cited, and is conformance claimed or only alignment recorded?
If the technique is cryptographic, is the key/secret retained such that the transform is reversible by the holder (NIST warning: not de-identification)?
Which source path (WM-DAT-004) does this treatment apply to, and does a WM-XCT-020 classification binding constrain minimum strength?
What technique-specific parameters apply (mask alphabet, generalisation hierarchy, bucket edges, rounding quantum, noise distribution, token format)?
Is the transform irreversible, reversible by the holder with separately kept secrets, or reversible by the recipient?
When a value is removed, is the member omitted, set null, replaced with a redaction token, or defaulted (align OData omit-values=nulls|defaults)?
If a record-level code is emitted for later re-identification by the holder (HIPAA 164.514(c)), is it stipulated as non-derived and is the mechanism forbidden from disclosure?
Does this policy apply a named identifier pack (HIPAA Safe Harbor 18, HIPAA limited data set 16, or a local pack), and under which jurisdiction?
If Safe Harbor is not used, is an expert-determination analysis referenced (164.514(b)(1)), and where is that evidence held?
If a limited data set is the grain, which WM-XCT-002 data-use agreement is referenced, and are residual city/state/ZIP and dates retained as specified by 164.514(e)(2)?
Has the holder attested they do not have actual knowledge that remaining data can identify an individual (164.514(b)(2)(ii)), and at what observation time?
What is the compiled template's identifier (master-system id, IRI, or Dimension UUID/ULID) and which policy version and source-schema version produced it?
Which paths and types appear in the consumer schema fragment, and how many source paths were omitted?
What self-describing handle (OData context URL analogue, GraphQL type name, FHIR profile) lets a recipient interpret the projected payload without out-of-band rules?
Which output media types / profiles is this template compiled for (application/json, application/fhir+json, application/vnd.api+json, application/json;odata.metadata=minimal)?
Which hash algorithm and canonicalisation (sorted path list, treatment params, grain, schema version) produce the shape fingerprint?
Must served instances carry an incomplete/SUBSETTED completeness token so they cannot overwrite full records?
Which fingerprint and policy-version fields MUST be supplied to WM-XCT-004 on each serve, without this model storing the trail?
Does the policy compile cleanly against the referenced source schema, and which paths are unknown, type-incompatible, or under-protected versus the classification binding?
Which referenced versions (schema, classification binding, cohort floor, policy) would invalidate this compiled template?
When was the template compiled (event time) and when was that fact observed/ingested (RFC 3339)?
To what is this policy attached: a WM-XCT-002 contract/grant, a source object type (WM-DAT-004), an audience/class of recipient, or a named request protocol?
What purpose hint must be compatible with the referenced grant so the shape remains the minimum necessary for that purpose?
Is this policy reusable across many bindings (one shape, many contracts/audiences), and which binding identifiers currently point at it?
Which WM-XCT-001 owner or steward is referenced as authorised to attach this shape (reference only)?
What is the inclusive effective window of this binding (RFC 3339 with offset or Z), and is open-ended end permitted?
What precedence or specificity hint should WM-KNW-012/XCT-038 use when multiple projection policies match, without this model combining them?
Is this shape limited to a named environment or location (query interface, enclave, public publish), as a parameter rather than an evaluation?

requirements: Resolve every provider-only bundle, layer and finding against primary evidence.
Resolve the model boundary and entry kind before accepting structure.
Verify live URLs and version pins for all accepted sources.
Record every rejected and deferred node with a reason.
Do not publish while any critical conflict remains unresolved.
